family.description: This entry represents the N-terminal TIM barrel domain of 3-dehydroquinate synthase II. This family includes members of 3-dehydroquinate synthase II ([ec:1.4.1.24]), encoded by aroB genes in M. maripaludis which is widely distributed in methanogens. In M. jannaschii, proteins ADTH synthase (AroA) and DHQ synthase II (AroB) are required to convert 6-deoxy-5-ketofructose-1-phosphate (DKFP) and aspartate semialdehyde to 3-dehydroquinate (DHQ) in vitro [[cite:PUB00109170],[cite:PUB00060486]].
family.name: 3-dehydroquinate synthase II N-terminal domain

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The paper identifies MJ1249 as Q58646; current v1 reference is361aa with PF01959 1-173 and PF26558 187-361, strain JAL-1/DSM2661/ATCC43067. MJ0400/Q57843 is a separate required assay partner; no PF01959 assignment is made for its activity. Historical plasmid sequences were not independently reconstructed.
causal_graphs.limitations: The output sums DHQ and its reported downstream DHB readout, not a pure DHQ yield. No isolated-domain sufficiency, cellular essentiality, residue-level chemistry or direct observation of every intermediate is established. MJ0400 preparation contained a small chloramphenicol-acetyltransferase contaminant. No replicate/error estimates or raw chromatograms were reviewed.

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Intact MJ1249/Q58646 v1 contains PF01959 1-173 and PF26558 187-361; MJ0400/Q57843 supplies a separate upstream activity. Full-protein and multienzyme context are not transferred to the isolated domain or to bacterial GriH.
causal_graphs.limitations: Qualitative product formation only. The paper reports330nmol for the NAD condition and150nmol for NADP, but330nmol exceeds the stated200nmol ASA and275nmol DKFP inputs; absolute yield and stoichiometry remain unresolved. The footnote says both in air and all samples under argon. Buffer and readout differ from rows1-3, so no clean cofactor fold-stimulation is inferred. NADH formation, transient intermediates and catalytic residues are not directly measured here.
